modern-features.summary: Know how ES modules load and link, how iterators and generators really step, and how symbols, Proxy and Reflect hook into the language. Interviews probe the edge cases: cycles, live bindings, next(arg) sequencing and Proxy invariants.
points: ES modules are strict, have `undefined` as top-level `this`, and load in phases: parse, link, then evaluate dependencies first. Imports are hoisted, live and read-only.
CommonJS exports are a plain object filled in as the file runs: destructuring copies values, and a require cycle returns a half-filled `exports`.
In ESM cycles, function declarations are usable before their module runs, but `let`, `const` and `class` exports throw a TDZ ReferenceError.
An iterator is an object with `next()`; `return()` is called on early exit (break, throw, destructuring that stops early), which is how generators run `finally`.
In a generator, each `next(arg)` answers the previous `yield`, so the first argument is discarded. `yield*` forwards values and evaluates to the delegate's return value.
Forward Proxy traps with `Reflect.*(target, key, receiver)` to keep getters and inheritance correct. Invariants make traps throw when they misreport locked properties.
`??=`, `||=` and `&&=` short-circuit the whole assignment, so setters do not run when no assignment is needed.
traps: A global regex keeps `lastIndex` between `test()` calls, so the same input can alternate between true and false.
Private fields and built-ins with internal slots (Map, Set, Date) break when a method is called with a Proxy as `this`.
`import()` resolves to the module namespace: the default export is `.default`, not the resolved value itself.
